projects.title: Underworld Geodynamics
projects.description: The Underworld geodynamics code: what it is, how to run it, and the Technical Notes series of methods, benchmarks and worked examples.

pages.title: Faults and patch-refinement of the mesh
pages.description: A slipping fault is a discontinuity the mesh has to represent, along a trace that moves as the model runs. We build the fault into a short-lived mesh made from a static base. The base holds the state, the partition and the coarse multigrid levels; the add-on is a copy of the base's finest level with the fault placed into it as a narrow structured band, split along the fault, and rebuilt from the base whenever the fault moves.

pages.title: Faults: to mesh or not to mesh?
pages.description: A fault is a discontinuity and a mesh represents continuity, so the first question is whether the fault has to go into the mesh at all. Shear bands and a painted director cost no mesh work; cutting and conforming cost a great deal. What each of the four representations asks of the mesh and of the constitutive model, where they agree, and why they part company at a junction.
